title: French negatives & questions
examples: When do I use ne pas versus est-ce que?
Can I use all three ways to ask a question?

explain.say: Today we will learn three ways to say no in French. We will also learn three ways to ask questions.

items: ne...pas is the basic negative form.
est-ce que is a simple question structure.

draw.text: Negatives: ne...pas; Questions: est-ce que, inversion

explain.say: The first way to make a sentence negative is using ne and pas. We place ne before the verb and pas after the verb.
For example, saying I speak French becomes je ne parle pas français. The 'ne' and 'pas' surround the verb.
The second way is using est-ce que. This structure keeps the word order the same. It is very easy to remember.
If I want to ask if you eat bread, I say Est-ce que tu manges du pain. The word order remains normal.

items: Step 1: Add Est-ce que (Est-ce que tu manges du pain)
End: Question Mark (?) (Est-ce que tu manges du pain ?)

draw.text: Est-ce que tu manges du pain ?

explain.say: The third way is inversion. This means we swap the subject pronoun and the verb. We use a hyphen to join them.

faq.q: When should I use ne pas?
faq.a: You use ne pas when you want to make a statement negative. It is the most common way to deny something in French.
asks: How do I say something is not true?
What is the negative form of a sentence?

faq.q: Is est-ce que always the best way to ask questions?
faq.a: No, est-ce que is good because it is simple. However, inversion and est-ce que are both correct options.
asks: Can I use est-ce que for every question?
Which question form is easiest for beginners?

faq.q: Does inversion always use a hyphen?
faq.a: Yes, when you invert the subject and the verb, you must use a hyphen. This connects the two words together.
asks: How do I join the verb and subject for a question?
Do I write a dash between the verb and subject?

faq.q: Can I mix these three methods?
faq.a: No, you should choose one method for the whole conversation. Stick to one structure to sound more natural.
asks: Is it okay to use est-ce que sometimes and inversion other times?
Should I switch between the three forms?

faq.q: What about verbs that change in tense?
faq.a: The ne...pas structure must agree with the verb's tense. You must remember the correct conjugation for the negative.
asks: Does the negative change the verb ending?
Is the negative form different for past tense?

facts: The negative structure always surrounds the main verb.
Est-ce que keeps the word order the same as a statement.
Inversion requires joining the verb and subject with a hyphen.
The word 'ne' is pronounced in most common French speech.

quiz.say: How do you say 'She does not sing' using ne...pas?
quiz.why: The structure requires 'ne' before the verb and 'pas' after the verb.

wrong.1: Placing 'pas' before the verb is incorrect word order.
wrong.2: The subject pronoun must come before the negative structure.
wrong.3: The 'pas' must follow the verb, not interrupt it.

quiz.say: Which structure is correct for asking 'Do you speak English?'?
quiz.why: Est-ce que is a reliable structure that keeps the word order simple.

wrong.1: This is inversion, which is a different structure.
wrong.2: The placement of 'est-ce que' is incorrect.
